best_architecture: Recommended pattern: a LangGraph-style StateGraph (directed graph of nodes + conditional edges over a shared, serializable State object) layered on top of a persistent Goal Tree, with a thread-id-scoped checkpointer writing snapshots to MongoDB. This combines three proven ideas: (1) Graph/state-machine control flow (LangGraph, Apache Burr) instead of linear chains. Nodes are pure functions `(state) -> partial_state_update`; edges are static (`add_edge`) or conditional (`add_conditional_edges(source, router_fn)`); a node may also return a `Command(update=..., goto=...)` to update state and route in one step. Conditional edges are the critical design element: a router function inspects current state and decides the next node, enabling branching, retries, error handling, and human-in-the-loop gates. (2) Hierarchical Goal Tree for task decomposition. Each goal node has id, parent_id, children[], a description, a status enum, and result/error fields. High-level goals decompose into ordered subgoals (cf. Plan-and-Solve, ReAcTree, HyperTree Planning). A goal is COMPLETED only when all children are COMPLETED; failure of a required child marks the parent BLOCKED/FAILED. This separates *what to do* (goal tree, slow-changing, the durable plan) from *how the agent is currently executing* (the state-machine cursor over that tree). (3) Durable persistence via a checkpointer. The whole graph State is serialized to a checkpoint after every node ('super-step') boundary, scoped by `thread_id` (one task/session = one thread) and ordered by `checkpoint_id`. To resume, load the latest checkpoint for the thread_id and replay/continue from the last completed node. This delivers the three Local-Claw requirements directly: checkpoint progress, resume after interruption/crash, and graceful error handling (replay from last good checkpoint rather than restarting; route to a recovery/compensation node on failure). Key design decisions that matter most: (a) State must be JSON-serializable end to end -- no functions, streams, or circular refs in state; store only plain data and references (cf. LangGraph blob table for oversized values). (b) Make node transitions idempotent so a replayed checkpoint after a crash does not double-execute side effects (write a step-completed marker before performing irreversible actions; see SagaLLM transactional/compensation pattern for rollback). (c) Use an explicit status enum on every goal node: PENDING -> IN_PROGRESS -> COMPLETED | FAILED | BLOCKED, with timestamps, attempt counts, and a result/error payload. (d) Separate short-term state (the checkpointed graph state for resume) from long-term memory (a vector/document store of past results, AutoGPT/BabyAGI style) so the checkpoint stays small. (e) Prefer event-driven state updates (write checkpoint at each node/super-step boundary, i.e. on a real state-transition event) over polling; reserve polling for external watchers (a UI or supervisor) reading the checkpoint store. For Local-Claw specifically (MongoDB-backed, long-running multi-step tasks): use LangGraph's StateGraph with the official `langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb` MongoDBSaver (supports thread_id scoping, TTL, human-in-the-loop, time-travel, fault tolerance, and auto-propagation to subgraphs), store the Goal Tree as a field/collection keyed by thread_id, and keep large artifacts (file contents, long outputs) out of the inline checkpoint via references. If a lighter, framework-free, highly-observable alternative is preferred, Apache Burr offers the same explicit-state-machine model with built-in state snapshots, replay, and a debugging UI. [uncertain: exact MongoDB document schema is design-dependent; the checkpoint internals described (checkpoints/blobs/migrations tables) are from the LangGraph Postgres saver and the MongoDB saver organizes data into collections analogously rather than identically]
reference_papers: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models (Yao et al. 2022/2023) - arxiv:2210.03629 - interleaves reasoning 'thoughts' with actions; the canonical step loop underlying most agent state machines

Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning (Shinn et al. 2023) - arxiv:2303.11366 - self-reflection memory buffer enabling error recovery / learning from failed transitions across episodes
Plan-and-Solve Prompting (Wang et al. 2023) - arxiv:2305.04091 - explicit plan-then-execute decomposition of a goal into ordered subtasks; basis for separating plan (goal tree) from execution

ReAcTree: Hierarchical LLM Agent Trees with Control Flow for Long-Horizon Task Planning (2025) - arxiv:2511.02424 - decomposes a goal into a dynamically constructed agent tree with control-flow nodes; directly maps to a persistent Goal Tree with status tracking

Enhancing LLM-Based Agents via Global Planning and Hierarchical Execution / GoalAct (2025) - arxiv:2504.16563 - global planning plus hierarchical execution to avoid local-branch lock-in in long-horizon tasks
HyperTree Planning: Enhancing LLM Reasoning via Hierarchical Thinking (2025) - arxiv:2505.02322 - hierarchical tree-structured planning beyond single-level decomposition

Task Memory Engine (TME): Enhancing State Awareness for Multi-Step LLM Agent Tasks (2025) - arxiv:2504.08525 (related: arxiv:2505.19436) - DAG-based spatial task memory; TRIM module decomposes inputs into subtasks and tracks state for robust multi-step execution

SagaLLM: Stateful, Disruption-Aware Orchestration (2025) - arxiv:2503.11951 [uncertain: arxiv id] - transactional Saga protocol with checkpointing, validation, compensation, and rollback giving ACID-like guarantees for multi-agent workflows; key reference for crash/error recovery semantics
Architecting Resilient LLM Agents: A Guide to Secure Plan-then-Execute Implementations (2025) - arxiv:2509.08646 - resilient plan-then-execute design patterns relevant to state-machine error handling
reference_repos: langchain-ai/langgraph - de facto standard library for building stateful, graph/state-machine LLM agents (StateGraph, nodes, conditional edges, checkpointers, durable execution, human-in-the-loop, time-travel) - https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph

langchain-ai/langchain-mongodb - contains langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb (MongoDBSaver) for persisting LangGraph state to MongoDB with TTL; directly relevant to Local-Claw's MongoDB requirement - https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-mongodb

apache/burr (DAGWorks Burr) - dependency-free Python state-machine library for stateful, observable agents with built-in state snapshots, replay/debugging UI, and pluggable persistence - https://github.com/apache/burr

Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT - early autonomous agent with multi-layer memory (short-term, long-term vector store, file-based) and cross-session persistence; reference for goal decomposition + execution-history state - https://github.com/Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT

yoheinakajima/babyagi - minimal (~140 LOC) task-driven autonomous agent: task-queue loop (create -> execute highest-priority -> generate new tasks -> reprioritize) with vector-store memory; cleanest reference for a persistent task queue / goal list - https://github.com/yoheinakajima/babyagi

crewAIInc/crewAI - role-based multi-agent orchestration framework with task assignment and memory; useful contrast for delegated-state vs explicit state-machine designs - https://github.com/crewAIInc/crewAI
key_libraries: langgraph - Python (also langgraph.js for TypeScript) - core state-machine/graph orchestration: StateGraph, nodes, conditional edges, BaseCheckpointSaver, durable execution. Primary recommendation for Local-Claw. Install: pip install langgraph
langgraph-checkpoint - Python - base checkpointer interface (BaseCheckpointSaver) and serialization protocol (SerializationProtocol); foundation all savers implement

langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb - Python (current ~0.4.0) - MongoDBSaver: persists StateGraph checkpoints to MongoDB, thread_id scoping, TTL, human-in-the-loop, time-travel, fault tolerance, subgraph auto-propagation. Install: pip install -U pymongo langgraph langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb. (npm equivalent: @langchain/langgraph-checkpoint-mongodb)

langgraph-checkpoint-postgres - Python - PostgresSaver / AsyncPostgresSaver alternative backend (checkpoints + checkpoint_blobs + checkpoint_migrations tables); use if Postgres is preferred over MongoDB
pymongo - Python - official MongoDB driver required by the MongoDB checkpointer and for storing the Goal Tree / long-term memory collections

burr - Python (~0.x, Apache incubating) - alternative explicit state-machine framework with @action functions, transitions, state snapshots, replay, and observability UI. Install: pip install 'burr[start]'
pydantic - Python (v2) - typed, JSON-serializable State and Goal-tree schema definitions (alternative to TypedDict) ensuring checkpointable state and clean (de)serialization
langchain-mongodb - Python - MongoDB-backed long-term memory / retrieval (LangGraph Store, vector retrieval tools) to complement short-term checkpoint state
chromadb / faiss-cpu - Python - open-source vector stores for long-term memory of past task results (BabyAGI/AutoGPT pattern); keeps large recall data out of the inline checkpoint
uncertain: Exact MongoDB checkpoint document/collection schema for Local-Claw is design-dependent; documented checkpoint internals (checkpoints/checkpoint_blobs/checkpoint_migrations) are from the LangGraph Postgres saver, and the MongoDB saver stores analogous data in collections rather than identical tables
